given: Triangle ABC with line DE parallel to BC
D lies on AB, E lies on AC
construction: Join BE and CD. Draw DM ⟂ AC and EN ⟂ AB (heights for area ratios).

steps.reason: Same height EN for bases AD and DB

steps.step: [1M] Area(ΔADE) = (1/2) × AE × DM and Area(ΔCDE) = (1/2) × EC × DM
steps.reason: Using AC as base; same height DM
Triangles on same base DE and between same parallels DE and BC are equal in area

commonMistakes: Skipping construction lines in the diagram.
Not writing the 'same base and between same parallels' area property.
Not naming the theorem in the final line.
examinerNotes: Even if you remember the proof, write it cleanly: Given → To Prove → Construction → Proof → Hence proved.
Use consistent triangle naming: ΔBDE and ΔCDE (avoid swapping letters).

given: Vertical pole height = 6 m, shadow = 4 m
Tower shadow = 28 m at the same time
construction: Draw two right triangles: (pole, shadow) and (tower, shadow). Mark the sun ray angle same.

steps.reason: Vertical object to ground makes right angle
Angle of elevation of sun is same at the same instant

commonMistakes: Using ratio directly without proving similarity.
Wrong correspondence of sides (height with shadow swapped).
examinerNotes: Write the similarity line explicitly; it is a mark by itself.
Mention CPST before substitution for full credit.

commonMistakes: Taking EC = x without using AC = AE + EC correctly.
examinerNotes: Alternative accepted: AD/AB = AE/AC after proving triangles similar.

given: Perpendicular from B meets hypotenuse AC at D

steps.step: [1M] From CPST: AB/AC = AD/AB ⇒ AB² = AD·AC
[1M] From CPST: BC/AC = DC/BC ⇒ BC² = DC·AC

commonMistakes: Not stating similarity triangles before CPST.
Mixing up AD and DC in the final addition.
Forgetting to mention D lies on AC.
examinerNotes: This is a standard board-proof approach via similarity; neat and high-scoring.
If you write the final line clearly, you secure the conclusion mark.
